videos.script: You can send an answer back to the model that wrote it, and ask whether it is right. It sounds like a second opinion. It is the same reader, reading twice. {{review}} This lesson measures what that second reading catches. On seventy answers at temperature zero, it flags eleven, and eight of them really are wrong. It finds eight of the fourteen mistakes. {{table}} The six it misses have something in common. Each one is a mistake the model would make again, so the answer looks right to it. {{misses}} Then you check a sampled run instead, and it catches far more. Sampling makes slips, and a slip is exactly what a reader that knows its own mind can see. {{slips}} On one message it does worse than miss. It talks a right answer back into the wrong one. {{argue}} By the end you know what to check with code, what to leave to the model, and how to measure the part you leave. {{close}}
